Create a project skill (slash command) that AUDITS the manuscript's sourced derivation for
  verification/best-practices compliance and emits a flag-only report. Read-only: it diagnoses and
  flags, it never edits.

  Working repo: C:\Users\marcu\git-repositories\mi-spectral (a citation-disciplined, AI-assisted
  JAIGP theory paper). Primary audit target: manuscript/derivation.qmd (the "canonical sourced
  derivation"); the skill should also accept manuscript/mi-spectral.qmd or any manuscript/*.qmd.

  STEP 0 — Use the skill-creator skill to scaffold this, and FIRST read these to ground every
  check in the repo's real conventions (do not infer them — read them):
    - CLAUDE.md  (the "Citation discipline (load-bearing)" + "Proposing references" sections)
    - .claude/hooks/check_citations.py  (the exact edit-time rule the audit must mirror)
    - todo/001-literature-and-hooks.md  (citation infrastructure) and
      todo/003-references-to-acquire.md (the proposed→queued→acquired→verified→cited lifecycle)
    - one literature/<citekey>.md  (the YAML frontmatter schema: citekey, authors, year, title,
      venue, doi, source_pdf, pdf_sha256, converted_via, last_synced — and the body = the actual
      converted paper text)
    - manuscript/derivation.qmd  (study its idioms: ::: {.column-margin} "Source." notes carrying
      an equation/theorem number + a `:lineref` link into the literature/ copy + a verbatim snippet;
      step tags [derived]/[mc]/[cited]; D-/R-/L-/A-tags; Appendix A verbatim source passages
      (#sec-src-*); Appendix B inline ```{python} lst-mc-* blocks with `assert`s)
    - verification/run_all.R + one _modules/*.R + a verification/cache/**/summary.csv  (the
      reproducibility layering: phases, standalone diagnostics, committed RDS+CSV caches)
    - literature/mi-spectral-better-bibTeX.bib  (source of truth for citekeys)

  WHAT THE SKILL CHECKS (report each finding with file:line, a one-line description, the evidence
  or its absence, a severity, and a suggested fix):

  A. Citation integrity (mechanical).
     - Every real bibliography citekey `@<citekey>` in the doc has BOTH a backing
       literature/<citekey>.md AND an entry in the .bib. Missing backing = BLOCKER (this is the
       load-bearing rule the hook enforces).
     - CRITICAL — do NOT flag Quarto cross-references as citations: `@eq-*`, `@sec-*`, `@lst-*`,
       `@fig-*`, `@tbl-*`, `@thm-*` are internal refs, not bib keys. (The existing lit_sync.py
       false-positives on these; the skill must correctly exclude them by resolving them against
       the doc's own {#label} definitions.)
     - Flag every `@TODO:<slug>` placeholder as an unresolved drafting citation.

  B. Evidence ↔ external exact text (the load-bearing, anti-hallucination check).
     - For each "Source." margin note: the `:lineref` must resolve to a real line in the named
       literature/<citekey>.md, and the verbatim snippet beside it must actually appear (exact or
       near-exact substring) in that file. Flag broken linerefs and snippets-not-found-in-source.
     - For each claim attributed to a citation (the equation/theorem number it cites), check the
       literature/<citekey>.md actually contains that equation/result and that the claim made about
       it in the derivation is supported by the source text — not just that the paper is cited.
       Mismatch or unverifiable attribution = BLOCKER. (This is the user's "evidence tangibly
       validated based on external exact text".)
     - Flag external/non-trivial assertions that carry NO source pointer and are not marked
       [derived], and [derived] steps that secretly lean on an external result.

  C. Reproducibility / simulation validation.
     - Every empirical/numerical claim (a number, "the simulation confirms", "phase-N", "the cache
       gives") must point to a reproducible artifact that EXISTS: a verification/*.R script, a
       run_all.R phase, or a verification/cache/**/{summary.csv,*.rds}. Flag numbers with no
       reproducible pointer, and pointers to missing files.
     - Each [mc] tag must have a corresponding Appendix-B ```{python} lst-mc-* block that contains
       a real `assert`. Flag [mc] tags with no backing assert.
     - Flag an "exact"/symbolic claim that is backed ONLY by Monte Carlo, or an O(1)/asymptotic
       claim backed only by a finite-n point — i.e., evidence-type vs claim-type mismatch.

  D. Internal consistency.
     - Every `@eq-/@sec-/@lst-` cross-ref resolves to a defined {#label}. Flag dangling refs.
     - The headline result is stated consistently across intro / theorem / combine (flag
       contradictions in the stated equation or its scope conditions, e.g. MCAR-only vs general).

  E. Honesty / over-claiming.
     - Flag "proved/exact/for any regular family/general" where the doc's own scope notes say
       "asserted", "spot-checked", "to leading order", "O(n^-1)", or "MVN instantiation". Surface
       any claim that outruns its stated verification.
     - Flag house-jargon in outside-reader-facing prose per the project's style ban
       (ledger / numerical witness / tagged / machine-checked / Stage N / consume) — INFO severity.

  F. Reference lifecycle hygiene.
     - Cross-check each cited citekey against todo/003: a key cited in manuscript/ but not marked
       `verified`/`cited` there is a WARN (cited-but-not-logged-as-verified).

  OUTPUT: a single markdown report grouped by severity (BLOCKER / WARN / INFO), each finding as
  `<file>:<line> — <issue> — evidence: <found/'snippet not in source'/'no cache'> — fix: <…>`,
  preceded by a one-line PASS/FAIL summary and per-dimension counts. Read-only: never modify the
  manuscript or literature files. Accept an optional argument for the target file (default
  manuscript/derivation.qmd).

  SKILL MECHANICS:
     - Project skill under .claude/skills/<name>/ (suggested name: derivation-audit; finalize via
       skill-creator). Slash command, e.g. /derivation-audit [path].
     - The semantic claim↔source check (B) is the hard part and may warrant reading each cited
       literature/<citekey>.md and matching per-claim; design it to be thorough but bounded
       (it can fan out per citation if helpful).

  TEST before finishing: run the skill on manuscript/derivation.qmd and confirm it (1) flags any
  genuine gaps, (2) does NOT false-positive on @eq-/@sec-/@lst- cross-references, (3) confirms the
  Shimodaira/Cavanaugh/Claeskens/Hens/Kenward citekeys resolve to literature/ files, and (4)
  correctly pairs each [mc] tag with its lst-mc-* assert. Report what it found on that first run.
